cohort: 392 sepsis-suspected newborns admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit of Hawassa University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital from March 2021 to November 2021
finding: The prevalence of sepsis caused by bacteria among newborns was 36.5%, with Klebsiella species being the predominant bacteria (42.65%), followed by non-lactose fermenting Gram-negative bacteria (18.88%) and Enterococcus species (18.18%), and high levels of antimicrobial resistance were observed among Gram-negative bacteria.
